name: South Vietnam (Ho Chi Minh City · Mekong Delta)

language.script_notes: Khmer script also turns up on temples and signs in the western Mekong Delta, near the Cambodian border.

road_furniture.bollard_shape: Concrete post; verify profile against photos.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam on highways; long delta roads run on embankments beside canals with low kerbs instead.
road_furniture.line_paint: White and yellow centre lines where marked; red-and-white striped sign poles.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted black-and-white kerbs in towns and along canal-side roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Southern power company (EVN SPC): concrete poles carrying a 'mountain + inverted-triangle' mark, frequently doubled by a parallel line of fibre-optic poles — a checkable 'this is the south' tell. Yellow-topped kilometre stones on highways.

architecture.roof_style: Tube-house frontages; wider streets and more modern mid-rise in Ho Chi Minh City.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal, concrete slab, some tile.
architecture.wall_construction: Masonry tube houses, often brightly painted; canal-side houses on low stilts or piles over the water in the delta.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Vivid saturated colours; mustard-yellow French colonial in central Saigon.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Colourful tube houses; grand French colonial set-pieces in Saigon (Notre-Dame, Central Post Office, Opera House); Khmer Theravada pagodas and Cao Đài temples in the delta; stilt houses over canals.

nature.vegetation: The Mekong Delta is a web of rivers and canals lined with coconut and water palms, banana and intense green rice; mangroves near the coast; rubber plantations in the south-east around Đồng Nai and Bình Dương.
nature.terrain: Almost entirely flat — the vast, low, waterlogged Mekong Delta crisscrossed by channels, plus the slightly higher south-east. Phú Quốc island has unpaved red-earth roads.
nature.climate_signature: Hot and humid all year with a pronounced wet and dry season and no cool winter. Strong tropical light, deep greens, palm shadows.

vehicles.plate_format: DDLL-NNN.NN; province codes 50–59 are Ho Chi Minh City, 60s–90s cover the southern provinces.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Motorbike swarms, densest of all in Ho Chi Minh City; boats do much of the transport work in the delta.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Moped-mounted and trekker imagery. Scenes are consistently hot, bright and green — no grey winter look anywhere in the south.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — Vietnamese script, tube houses, motorbikes, red flags
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The south is flat tropical delta, hot and green year-round, with 'mountain + inverted-triangle' EVN SPC poles and parallel fibre-optic poles; the north is hilly with karst, a cool grey winter and holed EVN NPC poles.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The Mekong lowlands, palms, rice and Theravada temples continue straight across the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Vietnamese Latin script vs Khmer script; southern Vietnam is more densely built and developed, with far more motorbikes and painted tube houses.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Hot tropical lowland, Buddhist temples, palms
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Thailand drives on the left and uses Thai script; Vietnam drives on the right with Latin script and much denser motorbike traffic.
